requirement: A `{req}` definition MUST use an opening fence of at least three colons immediately followed by `{req} <name>`. A closing fence MUST have at least as many colons as the opening fence and nothing else on its line except whitespace. As in CommonMark fences, an opening or closing fence MAY be indented by up to three spaces; a line indented by four or more spaces MUST NOT be a fence. The requirement body MUST be all Markdown between those fence lines, including headings, examples, diagrams, and blank lines, except for the header option lines of {cite}`requirements.references.anchors`, and MUST NOT include text after the closing fence. Leading and trailing whitespace MUST be excluded when comparing the body with evidence.
rationale:
I found no gaps. Every obligation in `requirements.ci.span` has code that carries it out and a test that asserts its outcome.

**Code.** `src/evidence.rs#fn[collect_definitions]` carries the {impl} reference. It calls `definition_blocks` and `without_options` (both in `src/lib.rs`), and `colon_fence` is reached through `definition_blocks`.

**Obligations, code and tests**

- **Opening fence.** It needs at least three colons immediately followed by `{req} <name>`.
  - `src/lib.rs#fn[colon_fence]` requires a colon run of 3 or more.
  - `definition_blocks` then requires the suffix to start with `{req}` and requires whitespace before a valid name.
  - Tests: `closing_fences_allow_no_trailing_text_and_fences_allow_three_spaces_of_indent` rejects `::{req}`, `::: {req}` and `:::{req}ready`.
- **Closing fence.**
  - It needs at least as many colons as the opening fence and nothing else on its line except whitespace. `definition_blocks` finds it with `count >= fence_length && suffix.trim().is_empty()`.
  - Tests: `closing_fences_allow_no_trailing_text_...` shows `:::foo` does not close and `::: ` does. `a_longer_colon_fence_contains_a_shorter_nested_directive` shows a shorter `:::` does not close `::::`.
- **Indentation.** `colon_fence` accepts up to 3 leading spaces and returns None for 4 or more. The same test covers a 3-space opening and closing fence, a 4-space opening that is not a fence, and a 4-space closing fence that does not close.
- **Body.** It is all Markdown between the fence lines, including headings, examples, diagrams and blank lines.
  - `definition_blocks` sets `body_start` to the line after the opening fence and `body_end` to the start of the closing fence line.
  - Fence-like lines inside code blocks are skipped via `code_block_ranges` and `overlaps_protected`.
  - Tests: `colon_requirement_span_includes_markdown_and_excludes_following_text` covers a code block containing `:::`, ATX and Setext headings, and blank lines. `a_longer_colon_fence_contains_a_shorter_nested_directive` asserts the exact body slice.
- **Header option lines excluded.** `without_options` removes the option ranges recorded by `definition_blocks`. `anchor_options_are_metadata_not_body_text` and `anchored_files_must_be_completely_covered_and_resolvable` test this.
- **No text after the closing fence.** The block ends at the closing fence line. The span test places "Outside the requirement." after the fence and expects the evidence to match without it. `a_longer_colon_fence_...` also asserts `Outside.` lies after the block end.
- **Whitespace excluded in comparison.** `collect_definitions` applies `.trim()` to the body. `requirement_bodies_are_compared_without_surrounding_whitespace` tests this.
  - The evidence text is compared exactly against the trimmed body in `validate_evidence_file`. I read "excluded" as applying to the body, so I did not count this as a gap.
- **Missing closing fence.** `closed: false` is recorded and reported by `collect_definitions`. `reports_a_missing_closing_colon_fence` tests this. The text does not require this error, but `requirements.ci.definition_errors` does, and the same code marks {impl} for it.

All the tests listed above carry {test} references to `requirements.ci.span`. I did not reassess the cited `requirements.references.anchors`. The code ignores option lines in the body, which is consistent with it.

text: A `{req}` definition MUST use an opening fence of at least three colons immediately followed by `{req} <name>`. A closing fence MUST have at least as many colons as the opening fence and nothing else on its line except whitespace. As in CommonMark fences, an opening or closing fence MAY be indented by up to three spaces; a line indented by four or more spaces MUST NOT be a fence. The requirement body MUST be all Markdown between those fence lines, including headings, examples, diagrams, and blank lines, except for the header option lines of {cite}`requirements.references.anchors`, and MUST NOT include text after the closing fence. Leading and trailing whitespace MUST be excluded when comparing the body with evidence.
A `{req}` declaration MAY list `:impl:` and `:test:` options, and an `{example}`
declaration MAY list `:test:` options, immediately after its opening fence and
before its body, one per option line, naming a project file path or
{cite}`requirements.references.outline_selectors`. Each anchor MUST be an `{impl}` or `{test}` edge, under
{cite}`requirements.references.roles`, from the definition to the anchored file or
node, for files that cannot or should not carry a reference themselves.
Paths MUST follow the path rules in {cite}`requirements.ci.schema`. Option lines
MUST NOT form part of the definition's text for evidence comparison or for
requirements inputs, and MUST NOT render as body text.
An anchored file or node MUST be covered by the definition's evidence under
{cite}`requirements.references.evidence_coverage`, by an input selecting it, so changing the file makes that evidence stale. A path or selector that
does not resolve to a readable, permitted file or node MUST be a validation error naming the
definition and the path; authoring MUST report it before inference, because the
definition cannot be assessed without it. Any other option line in a `{req}` or
`{example}` declaration MUST be a validation error.
